observations:
LM2 Torah 108 is a two-sentence aphorism — one of the shortest entries in Likutay Moharan. The full text reads: 'Once [the Rebbe] spoke about human affairs, and said: A person, for a single small pleasure of a quarter hour, can lose and forfeit all of this world together with the World to Come.' He then repeated this in Yiddish.

The teaching contains no bechina language (no 'X הוא בחינת Y', no 'X נקרא Y', no conceptual equivalences). The only relationship present is a causal/eitza one: yielding to a moment of trivial pleasure leads to the loss of eternal goods. This is pure moral exhortation, not a conceptual topology of equated ideas.

There are two concepts mentioned — תַּעֲנוּג קָטָן (a small/trivial pleasure) and אֲבֵידַת הָעוֹלָמוֹת (the loss of worlds) — but they stand in a cause-and-effect (eitza) relationship, not a bechina (shared-nature) relationship. A package requires 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain; that condition is not met here.

Conclusion: NO_NEW_PACKAGES. The dataset correctly has zero entries for reference 1108, and there is nothing in the source text that warrants adding any.
